name: read-aloud
desc: Free, open-source text-to-speech reader for Windows — narrate documents and clipboard with SAPI voices offline. 100 MB portable, MIT.
features: ✅ **Reads real documents** — opens TXT, EPUB, DOCX and PDF text, keeps reading position per file
✅ **Clipboard hotkey** — Win+Alt+S narrates whatever was just copied, then returns to what you were doing
✅ **Sentence highlighting** — the current sentence is highlighted in the text pane while it is spoken
✅ **Voice and speed control** — any installed SAPI voice, 0.5x to 3x rate, pitch and volume per document
✅ **Export to audio** — renders a document to WAV or MP3 in the background for commutes
✅ **Offline by design** — no cloud voices, no network, no account; your documents stay local
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, portable, MIT with SHA-256 releases
compare: | EPUB and DOCX support | **Yes** | Yes | DOCX only | No |
| Offline with SAPI voices | **Yes** | Yes | Cloud voices | Yes |
| Audio export WAV and MP3 | **Yes** | Yes | Paid tier | No |
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Zip | Web or app | With OS |
faqQ: how to make Windows read text out loud for free?
faqA: Narrator is built for screen control, not for reading a document to you, and cloud readers stop the moment the connection does. read-aloud uses the SAPI voices already on the machine, tracks your position per file, and can render long documents to MP3 offline. It is a 100 MB portable exe under MIT, no account, no telemetry.
s1: Dark reader (#121417, warm amber #FBBF24): text pane with sentence highlight, voice dropdown Microsoft David, rate slider at 1.4x.
s2: Library and position view: recent documents with progress bars, five-minute-rule timer chip, resume banner on one EPUB.
s3: Export panel: WAV and MP3 options, chapter split toggle, queue of two documents rendering, output folder and bitrate fields.
